meaning_fixes.before: <op()><sp(20)>The Siberian Railway... they're the dome police.<ab(500)><ed()>
meaning_fixes.after: <op()><sp(20)>The Siberian Railway... they're the Domepolis police.<ab(500)><ed()>
meaning_fixes.reason: The source word romanized as 'Domu Porisu' is a locked corpus proper noun, already translated 'Domepolis' with a King Gainer Wikipedia source in work/translation/en/encyclopedia_021_b.json and encyclopedia_022.json. The draft read it as a plain adjective ('dome') describing a generic 'police' force instead of using the established name; restored it.

meaning_fixes.before:
<sp(20)>We don't know its size or numbers,
but please be careful, everyone!<ab(800)><ed()>
meaning_fixes.after:
<sp(20)>We don't know its composition or numbers,
but please be careful, everyone!<ab(800)><ed()>
meaning_fixes.reason: The source word romanized 'kousei' means composition/makeup (what units the force is made of), not size. Translating it as 'size' duplicated the following word for 'numbers' and lost the distinct piece of information the source gives.

The source word 'Invader' (katakana loanword) is a proper-noun faction from this game's own Getter Robo Armageddon lore: encyclopedia_022.json translates the linked book(49) term as 'Invaders', tied to the 'Moon Invader War' and Dr. Saotome's Shin Dragon -- the same Shin Dragon that reactivates at the end of this mission (row 4530). Lowercasing it turned a named-faction jab into a generic insult; capitalized to match the established term.

meaning_fixes.before: <op()><sp(20)>Typical man, playing dumb when it's convenient!<ab(500)><ed()>
meaning_fixes.after: <op()><sp(20)>Typical man, playing dumb when it's inconvenient!<ab(500)><ed()>
meaning_fixes.reason: The source phrase means 'when it becomes inconvenient (for him)', not 'convenient'. The draft inverted the condition under which the man feigns ignorance -- a reversed-meaning error.

checked_decisions.finding: Gekko ship-name usage confirmed consistent with the locked glossary spelling; no meaning issue.
Siberian Railway Overman pursuer's dialogue confirmed coherent; speaker kept nameless/gender-neutral since the source never names him in this row range.

Turn-taking re-verified via the <ab()>/<ed()> continuation markers: 4425-4426 is the pursuer blaming Gain for the Exodus (one box); 4427 is Gain retorting he can't afford to be caught (new box, separate speaker); 4428 is the pursuer's threat naming Gain's 'Black Southern Cross' nickname; 4429-4430 is the pursuer retreating after failing twice and vowing to catch them. No reversal or misattribution found.

Row 4448's idiom for being fired/dismissed is correctly rendered as 'you'll be fired', kept distinct from the literal neck-breaking threat in row 4468 ('I'll snap that neck of yours'); the draft's own note comparing the two is confirmed correct.
One continuous display box: Boone argues the 'womanizer' label is simplistic, then gives his name, 'Asuham Boone!' -- confirmed as self-introduction, not a third party naming him.

The unidentified enemy at 4455-4459 is kept as 'its'/gender-neutral (pilot not yet revealed); by 4460-4461 it is confirmed to be Asuham Boone's Power Golem, whose Overskill (one word, per ruling) is superhuman strength. No premature gendering or invented identity found.
Source row ends with the malformed, unpaired <ed(500)> (no matching <ab()>); kept exactly as in the source per the ruling to preserve malformed commands rather than repair them.

Karin is referred to only as 'Karin' / 'my sister' in this slice's actual dialogue text; the fuller identification 'Karin Boone, Asuham's sister' is glossary-level research, not text present in these rows, so no dialogue text needed to change to match the accepted full name.

uncertainties.issue: The Siberian Railway Overman pursuer in 4420-4431 is never named in the source text itself. The role fits Yassaba Jin (Siberian Railway squad commander, character_names_021.json) but this cannot be confirmed from this row range alone; kept gender-neutral ('that guy', 'they') as the draft already did. Not resolved by this review.

The 'Domepolis' fix is based on cross-referencing already-translated encyclopedia files (encyclopedia_021_b.json, encyclopedia_022.json) rather than the glossary files named in the task brief (terms_028.json, unit_names_014_a/b.json, character_names_021.json), where 'Domepolis' does not currently appear. Recommend adding 'Domepolis' to terms_028.json centrally so future dialogue slices use it consistently.

The task's ruling accepts 'Kids Munt' (King Gainer Wikipedia spelling), which batch_04478 already uses. However, work/translation/en/encyclopedia_022.json currently translates the same name as 'Kizz Munt' in two places (the Siberian Railway description). This is an existing corpus inconsistency outside this slice's scope (a different resource table); flagged for central reconciliation rather than edited here.
